title: Consecutive Login Days
description:
Find all users who logged in for at least 3 consecutive days.

Table `Logins`: `id (INT), user_id (INT), login_date (TEXT)`
output_format: Distinct user_id values who logged in 3+ consecutive days.

hidden_tests.input:
CREATE TABLE Logins (id INT, user_id INT, login_date TEXT);
INSERT INTO Logins VALUES (1, 5, '2024-02-10'), (2, 5, '2024-02-11'), (3, 5, '2024-02-12');

hints: Join the table three times for day 1, day 2, and day 3.
Match `user_id` and check that date offsets are +1 day and +2 days.

starter_code.sql:
-- Consecutive Login Days
-- Write your SQL query below
SELECT ...
FROM ...;
starter_code.python:
# Consecutive Login Days (SQL Problem)
# You can test via SQL query or Python

print('Run query in SQL tab')

reference_solution: SELECT DISTINCT l1.user_id FROM Logins l1 JOIN Logins l2 ON l1.user_id = l2.user_id AND date(l2.login_date) = date(l1.login_date, '+1 day') JOIN Logins l3 ON l1.user_id = l3.user_id AND date(l3.login_date) = date(l1.login_date, '+2 day');
